Maya L: Heads-up — CompetitorY announced "EdgeLite Quant" today. Claims ~60% lower serving cost using aggressive 4-bit quant and a small SDK for edge hosts. Were seeing a spike in RFPs mentioning "quant" and several trial accounts asking about on-prem cost parity. Thoughts?
Ethan G: Hmm. Two ways to react: try to match cost with a cheap tier (parity) or double-down on tooling (routing/pricing controls) so customers get better predictability without matching raw price.
Priya S: Parity feels risky; that invites margin pressure. Tooling + control could be our wedge: per-route SLOs, cost caps, and transparent unit-cost reporting.
Noah T: Eng POV: quant support is nontrivial. For safety we can upstream experimental 4-bit kernels in runtime, but support, eval, and fallbacks add weeks. Also compatibility matrix with third-party libs is a pain.
Katie Z: Marketing: if we go tooling-first, need a crisp line: "Reduce inference cost without sacrificing predictability." Docs + calculator to show customers tradeoffs.
Maya L: Agree on a tooling-first play, but need guardrail: if the market moves fast we might need a limited-price experiment. Can we do a short spike to estimate realistic unit-cost improvement from payload batching + cache tweaks before committing to quant?
Ethan G: Yes. Proposed spike: simulate 1M tokens/day baseline, run configs: (A) batching+cache tuning, (B) light quant flags on dev images, (C) routing cheap-variant to low-priority infra. Measure percent cost delta and failure modes. 10 working days.
Priya S: Launch criteria for any "lite-cost" offering: 1) end-to-end unit cost < 55% of baseline for target workload; 2) no >5% uptick in error rate for gen endpoints; 3) clear upgrade path to standard plan; 4) billing and SLA doc complete. If not met, we don't ship.
Noah T: Risk notes: 4-bit paths currently increase nondeterminism on some models — need quality evals per model family. Also: runtime flags need kill-switch for safemode.
Katie Z: Can Product produce two messaging frameworks? (A) "Cost-minimized prototyping" and (B) "Predictable low-cost production". We can test both in landing pages.
RoadmapBot: Telemetry event: "rpf_quant_mentions" = +28% week-over-week among trial accounts. Link: https://dash.redwood.example/telemetry/quant-signal
Maya L: Next steps: Ethan scope spike and eng owners, Priya draft acceptance tests + rollout runbook, Katie draft two landing page CTAs and pricing buckets for A/B. Reconvene in 8 business days. Keep updates here only.
Ethan G: Ill take the spike. ETA 8 business days. Will include perf matrix per model and cost projection.
Priya S: Ill write acceptance tests and an eval rubric for quality regressions.
Noah T: Ill prep runtime kill-switch and SRE monitoring playbook for the experiment.
Katie Z: Ill have landing CTAs and an initial pricing experiment plan ready for the reconvene.
Maya L: Cool. If telemetry moves faster we escalate. Thanks all — short updates only here.
